paragraphs: Subject: International Day. Dear Ravi, Thank you for your recipe. My mom wants to cook it on Sunday. I hope that you are well. Today I have a fact and a joke. The fact is that we had International Day at school on Friday. The joke is that I visited every table twice.

The school hall was full of color and music. Every class had a table about one country. Our class had a table about Singapore, your country. I drew a big poster that said "Welcome to Singapore." We put a flag and a map on it. We also put the photos from your school. Mia put the photos on a board, and Lily made a small paper flag. May wrote a short text about Palm Lake Primary School. Teacher Kim read it and smiled. I think that your class will like our table. May will send you the photos on Monday.

The class next to us had a table about Egypt. They made a big pyramid from paper, and it was as tall as Mia. They worked on it for three days. It had a small door, and three children sat inside. A funny guy from Tom's class wore a gold paper crown. He stood next to the pyramid and said, "I am the king!" Everybody took photos of him.

Each table also had a dish from its country. There was a small flag in every dish, so you knew which country it belonged to. I tasted food from six countries. Teacher Kim tasted a little of everything. One dish with red beans was very hot, so I drank two glasses of water. The food from our table was delicious, but I liked the sweet rice from the Thailand table best. My stomach was full, and my mouth was happy.

It was a perfect day for me. Next year, I want to bring a dish from Singapore. Which dish from Singapore do you like best? Please send me a photo of your International Day, too. Say hello to your class from all of us. Best wishes, Leo.
text.summary: Leo writes an email to his pen pal Ravi about International Day at school. Each class has a table about a country, and Leo tells Ravi about the tables, the food, and a paper pyramid.
